title: IAM Role Factory and Affinity Mapper for Private VPC deployments
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module (role-factory) that scaffolds least-privilege IAM roles, policies, and role bindings for Private (VPC) deployments, plus a lightweight 'affinity-mapper' helper (service-principal -> role mapping) and an upgrade/playbook for policy changes. The module should be opinionated about lifecycle (immutable role names + version tags), safe by default (deny-by-default examples), and integrate with our upgrade automation and drift detection tooling.

Scope and components:
- Terraform module 'redwood_priv_iam_role_factory' that: generates IAM roles, policy documents, optional service principals, and outputs role ARNs and canonical policy versions. Supports AWS IAM and an abstraction for GCP/other clouds (policy-json output).
- Affinity mapper: small, declarative mapping (map service-principal patterns -> role set) that can be used by our private deploy tooling to assign roles at provisioning time.
- Least-privilege policy templates and example transforms to convert high-level permissions (eg. 'kv-cache-access') into concrete actions.
- Upgrade/playbook: step-by-step process for changing policies (plan, canary apply to non-prod VPC, rollout to staging, promote to production), including Terraform state migration notes and versioned policy artifacts.
- Health checks: terraform plan gating in CI, periodic policy drift scans (example scripts that compare current IAM policies to desired state and alert via PagerDuty/Slack), and a small runtime check that validates role bindings exist for critical service principals during deploy.

Design constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Single module vs many small modules: We design a single role-factory with clear extension points rather than dozens of micro-modules to reduce cognitive overhead for SRE/SE teams. Extension points are provided via policy templates and JSON patches.
- Namespacing and immutability: Role names will include a short module-generated suffix and a version label; we avoid destructive renames by creating new versions and retiring old ones with a deprecation window. This increases role count but reduces accidental privilege revocation at runtime.
- Cross-account patterns: Support cross-account assume-role via role trust policies; provide example templates for centralized audit account and for Dedicated deployments.
- Cloud abstraction: Implement AWS-first with policy-json outputs for other clouds; fully multi-cloud policy generation is out of scope for this iteration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module lives in infra/terraform/modules/priv_iam_role_factory with README and examples.
- Module supports: role creation, policy attachment, service-principal aliasing, outputs role identifiers.
- Example affinity-mapper yaml shipped and referenced by private deploy templates.
- CI pipeline runs 'terraform plan' and fails on any diff that modifies production-bound roles without explicit 'allow-rollout' label in PR description.
- Upgrade playbook documented in Confluence and validated by running a canary update in our qa-vpc environment without service disruption.
- Automated drift check job created (cron) that posts findings to #priv-deploy-alerts and creates a ticket for critical drift.

Implementation notes and links:

- Draft Terraform module directory (internal): git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra.git//modules/priv_iam_role_factory

    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
      { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:GetObject"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-logs/*"] }
    ]
  }

Testing plan:
- Unit tests: terratest + local plan tests verifying generated policy JSON and output values.
- Integration: apply-to-qa (qa-vpc) using a dedicated apply runner with taints to simulate new role version creation.
- Canary rollout: apply change to 'canary' VPC used by non-critical customers, monitor role assume metrics and service auth failures for 24 hours.
- Post-deploy: run drift scanner and a synthetic auth test that assumes each role and performs a small read-only operation.

Rollout and rollback strategy:
- Create new role version instead of in-place mutation where possible.
- Canary apply to qa-vpc, if errors < 0.01% over 24h, proceed to staging.
- For production: staged rollout across regions using orchestration in private deployer with a 2-hour observation window per region.
- Rollback: revert to previous role version by re-attaching prior policy version and issue a corrective deploy; if rollback fails, escalate to SRE and open an incident with runbook.

Observability and health checks:
- IAM drift scanner (periodic job) that runs 'terraform plan' against a read-only state snapshot and diffs policies; alerts created with a severity mapping.
- Runtime check: deploy-time script validates that critical service principals have expected roles and logs mismatches.
- Metrics to track: policy-change-count, role-version-count, drift-warnings, canary-failures. Dashboards: private-console > IAM Health.

Security considerations:
- All policy artifacts must be stored in versioned storage (S3 with encryption and MFA-delete enabled) and signed.
- Module will support KMS-wrapped secrets for service principal keys; integration points documented.
- Security review required before GA for any module that grants wide actions (s3:*, iam:*).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide canonical naming convention for role vs resource tags across clouds.
- Finalize which high-level permissions should map to curated templates (eg. 'kv-cache-access').
- Determine retention window and automated retirement policy for stale role versions.

- Draft Confluence upgrade playbook and run canary in qa-vpc (Maya + SRE).
